page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 8 vCPUs and 30 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The compute capacity is backed by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, utilizing 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under dedicated CPU allocation. Hardware-level cache includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Instruction set flags include AVX, AES-NI, BMI2, and FMA, though modern extensions such as AVX-512, AMX, and SHA-NI are absent. The configuration does not include local storage disks, complimentary public IPv4 addresses, or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results place the computational capability of this instance in the lower tier relative to newer cloud offerings. In PassMark tests, the CPU achieved an overall score of 6,656.21 (average tier), with a physics score of 774.09 and encryption score of 2,705.33 (weak tier). Geekbench metrics mirror this profile, yielding a single-core score of 923.0 (bottom 10%) and a multi-core score of 3,531.0 (bottom 25%). Stress-ng evaluation confirms restrained execution, registering 1,113.08 in single-core and 5,835.33 in multi-core metrics. Throughput tests show low compression rates, with single-threaded gzip achieving 19.07 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression registering 6.95 GB/sec.

Memory throughput performs moderately better on sustained large blocks, recording uncached read speeds of 45.37 GB/sec and write speeds of 34.65 GB/sec, placing it within the middle 50% category. In contrast, small-block cached read throughput reaches 324.06 GB/sec (weak tier). Application workloads exhibit limited throughput, characterized by 4.56 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 5.27 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. For lightweight machine learning workloads, prompt processing on a small 135M parameter LLM executes at 327.51 tokens per second, with text generation reaching 100.1 tokens per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the older hardware class creates a clear tradeoff between standard resource footprint and per-core processing efficiency. While providing a balanced ratio of memory to compute suitable for legacy enterprise configurations, the instance lacks contemporary SIMD vector extensions and local disk throughput. Workload fit includes background processing, standard internal web serving, moderate batch automation, and non-intensive staging or database environments where high per-core execution speeds are not mandatory.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores, 2 threads per core) on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.3 GHz, paired with 30 GB of RAM. The instance features a 45 MB L3 cache and supports standard instructions including AVX and AES, but lacks newer vector extensions such as AVX-512. There are zero GPUs and no local storage volumes bundled with the configuration. In performance testing, the instance records lower-tier CPU metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 923.0 and multi-core score of 3,531.0, alongside moderate uncached memory bandwidth of 45.37 GB/sec read and 34.65 GB/sec write. Network and application benchmarks reflect basic capabilities, delivering 4.56 GB/sec in static web serving and 5.27 million operations/sec in Redis. It is suited for standard web application servers, moderate batch processing, and non-latency-critical legacy enterprise utilities.
